title: The Week, Unwrapped: Stuck Behind a Bus, Rigged by Machines, Lost at Minute Ten
dek: Democrats won the House and then lost a race to the House floor, the president found fraud in an election the polls saw coming, Arlington asked for quiet, and a rocket took 40 satellites with it.
body:
## Democrats Win the House, Lose a Footrace to It

One week after a historic midterm night, House Democrats got their first big chance to use their new swagger: a vote on Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. On Tuesday, the House voted 211 to 204 to refer the resolution to the Judiciary Committee, which effectively killed it for this Congress. [1] Eleven Democrats didn't vote in time. [1] Had all 11 voted no, the referral would have failed, 215 to 211. [1]

And the reasons! Rep. Melanie Stansbury's office said she was "blocked from entering the Capitol to vote due a traffic incident and a police escort of a bus." [1] Rep. Laura Gillen said she was stuck behind the same escort, Rep. Jonathan Jackson cited a traffic incident, and Rep. Marilyn Strickland's chief of staff said she missed it by one minute while waiting for a motorcade to pass. [1] The vote was scheduled for 15 minutes and held open for 29. [1]

Twenty-nine minutes. Entire civilizations have risen and fallen in less time than a House vote held open as a courtesy, and these are people who will soon be asking voters to trust them with oversight of the entire executive branch. (To be fair, seven Republicans skipped too, and one Democrat, Rep. Lou Correa, had announced his absence in advance for a medical procedure. [1]) The Democratic Party's new slogan, apparently: "We'll hold them accountable. Right after this bus."

## The President Has Reviewed the Election He Lost and Found It Rigged

Meanwhile, on the other side of the scoreboard, the president took about a week to discover that the midterms were crooked. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest," Trump posted on Monday, adding, "How could the Polls be so wrong???" [2]

Small problem: the polls weren't wrong. Most had forecast a strong Democratic night, and election officials said voting went reasonably smoothly, with no evidence of widespread fraud. [2] Trump's post also claimed "It's all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!" [2] which is a fascinating thing to say out loud about democracy.

What makes this one special is the reversal. Days earlier, in a 60 Minutes interview, he had seemed to accept the result and blamed the Iran war, gas prices and weak Republican candidates. [2] So the timeline is: concede, reflect, then decide the reflection was rigged too. Even Megyn Kelly's response was "Just stop." [2] When you've lost Megyn Kelly on a fraud claim, the machines aren't your problem.

## Senate Democrats Pick the Perfect Moment to Fight Each Other

Back on the winning side, Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced a challenge to Chuck Schumer for the job of leading the Senate. [3] Nothing says "we have a mandate" like spending the first fortnight of it arguing about who gets the big office.

To be clear, a leadership fight is a perfectly normal thing for a caucus to have. It's just that, between the bus and the ballot, the party's week went: win, miss the vote, start a leadership race. The other team's week went: lose, then call the loss fake. Somewhere a civics teacher is trying to explain both on the same worksheet.

## Hegseth's Arlington Moment

On Veterans Day, a sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier rebuked a group that included Pete Hegseth, his wife and aides after someone in the group laughed loudly enough to be heard. [4] The sentinel's line: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times." [4]

CBS News reported it's unclear who laughed or whether Hegseth himself made any noise. [4] The Pentagon's chief spokesman said "a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum." [4] Which is a very polite way of saying that the most composed person in the Defense Department's Veterans Day delegation was the one standing perfectly still with a rifle.

The bigger picture is that Hegseth started the week with an impeachment resolution aimed at him and ended it with that resolution in a Judiciary Committee drawer, [1] which means the man had a better week than the Democrats who were trying to impeach him.

## A Rocket, 40 Satellites and an Expensive Sunday

Finally, a reminder that space is hard. On Sunday, United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket suffered what the company called "an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit." [5] Forty Amazon Leo internet satellites were lost. [5] It was ULA's first outright mission failure since the company was formed in 2006, on only the fifth Vulcan flight. [5]

There had been warning signs: earlier flights in 2024 and February 2026 had problems with strap-on booster nozzles, and the Space Force paused national security launches on Vulcan while that was analyzed. [5] ULA's CEO said the company had identified three possible causes and addressed all of them; [5] Sunday's trouble showed up later, during the upper stage's burn. [5] Amazon has booked 38 Vulcan flights and needs more than 3,300 satellites to complete its constellation. [5] So, in the kindest possible terms: the company that can get you a phone charger by tomorrow morning would like you to know that orbit has a much longer delivery window.

## The Takeaway

This was a week in which the winners couldn't get to the floor, the loser couldn't accept the floor, and a rocket couldn't get past the tenth minute. [1] [2] [5] If there's a lesson, it's that power in Washington is less about what you win on election night and more about whether you show up on Tuesday. Leave earlier. Mind the bus.

pt.title: A Semana, Desembrulhada: Presos atrás de um ônibus, fraudados por máquinas, perdidos no minuto dez
pt.dek: Os democratas ganharam a Câmara e perderam a corrida até o plenário, o presidente achou fraude numa eleição que as pesquisas previram, Arlington pediu silêncio e um foguete levou 40 satélites junto.

de.title: Die Woche, ausgepackt: Hinter einem Bus festgesteckt, von Maschinen betrogen, in Minute zehn verloren
de.dek: Die Demokraten gewannen das Repräsentantenhaus und verloren dann das Rennen in den Plenarsaal, der Präsident fand Betrug in einer Wahl, die die Umfragen vorhersagten, Arlington bat um Ruhe, und eine Rakete nahm 40 Satelliten mit.
